title: The $200M Wall Painting: Equity vs. Cash

beats.say: In 2005, an artist was offered $60,000 cash or company stock for painting a startup’s office walls.
beats.visual: extreme low angle of a paintbrush on a ladder, neon office lights reflecting on wet wall, sodium glow from street below

beats.say: He chose the stock. That startup was Facebook.
beats.visual: silhouette of a painter at dusk, spray can in hand, backlit by a glowing blue digital billboard

beats.say: Most people would take the cash. It’s safe, immediate, and real.
beats.visual: close-up of a wad of $100 bills under cold fluorescent light, slight motion blur

beats.say: But that cash would’ve been gone by now. His stock? Worth over $200 million today.
beats.visual: extreme wide shot of Facebook HQ at night, tiny human figure walking toward it, fog in foreground

beats.say: The artist: David Choe. The job: graffiti murals for a growing company.
beats.visual: high angle of a spray-painted wall, paint dripping, single practical light casting long shadows

beats.say: Why risk it? Because ownership compounds. Cash spends once.
beats.visual: empty highway at night, one car’s taillights disappearing into the distance

beats.say: His $60,000 share became 0.1% of Facebook. That’s 200,000 shares at IPO.
beats.visual: extreme close of a stock certificate, edges slightly blurred, shallow depth of field

beats.say: At $100 a share in 2012, that was $20 million. Now? Over $200 million at $1,000 a share.
beats.visual: silhouette of a skyscraper against a stormy sky, rain-slick streets reflecting neon signs

beats.say: He didn’t just paint walls—he painted his future.
beats.visual: low angle of a half-finished mural, sunlight breaking through clouds, casting dramatic light on the wall

beats.say: The lesson? Sometimes the smartest move is betting on yourself.
beats.visual: extreme wide of a ridge line at blue hour, tiny figure standing at the edge, wind blowing their jacket

beats.say: Ownership in the right thing beats a safe paycheck every time.
beats.visual: high angle of a city at night, one streetlight illuminating a single parking meter, fog rolling in

beats.say: Cash is a payday. Equity is a dynasty.
beats.visual: extreme close of a gold fountain pen signing a document, ink well in shallow focus

beats.say: Follow for the money rules nobody taught you.
beats.visual: tower edge at night, city lights below, wind whipping past the camera

caption: He chose stock over $60K. Now it’s worth $200M. Ownership changes everything. #MoneyPsychology #EquityOverCash #GenerationalWealth #PersonalFinance
description: In 2005, artist David Choe took Facebook stock instead of $60K cash for painting their walls. Today, that stock is worth over $200M. The lesson: ownership compounds, cash spends. Always think long-term.
